PWN may be gamer slang for "own" but it's also short for Polskie Wydawnictwo Naukowe, Polish Scientific Publisher. It was a state-owned publishing house under "communism", one that published all encyclopedias, dictionaries, academic books and textbooks. It was privatized in 1991 and is still around. Their dictionary of the Polish language is still one of the two most authoritative in the country, along the online dictionary of Polska Akademia Nauk, Polish Academy of Sciences, a major state-owned research institution.

Somewhere along the way we've lost the difference between STAT and ASAP. 

STAT means immediately. ASAP is still important, it needs to get done promptly, but not immediately. They're not really synonyms -- it's like saying that NOW and SOON are interchangeable, which they are not.  They are different levels of urgency.

Naticked on OTT crossing MOTHRA.  Would of preferred OTT being clued as something like "Baseball player Mel" if that's what's needed to avoid a natick.  In other words, I'd rather have the crosswordese than the natick.  YMMV

My definition (YMMV) of a natick is a cross I have to guess at even though I have most if not all of the surrounding letters and I fully understand the context of the crossing clues.  Of course it will almost if not always be crossing proper nouns.

In this instance I am a casual sports fan who has no familiarity with Jordan OTT, who it turns out has just finished his 1st year as an NBA head coach, won 55% of his games and lost in the first round of the playoffs.

I also had no familiarity with MOTHRA, who it turns out is, well, moth-like.  If this clue had included some illusion to that, natick avoided. Words like "flying insect" or "lepidoptera" would at least have been something to point in the direction of "moth". No more than that expected given that it's Saturday.

Which brings up another point: no naticks, or whiffs of naticks please, ESPECIALLY easily avoidable ones (just think of it as an isolated incident calling for the use of "Mel" or "baseball" somehow, for Pete's sake), on any day of the week.  They compromise what makes crosswords truly elegant, that being that they are puzzles which offer loads of solving information beyond just one clue to one answer with a given number of letters.

[First full word sung in “The Alphabet Song”]

For those of us who care deeply about the fact that we still have to quietly hum the song to ourselves as we flip through the Unabridged OED, the use of “full word” here seems awkward. 

Some of us have suggested “double” (see earlier post(s)), which appears as W’s given name (and so if we called B ‘half-eight’ I suppose ‘half’ would have been mentioned). 

But if ‘double’, which is a word that is ‘sung’ as part of the name of one of the letters, could be the answer, then wouldn’t ‘A’ be the first, since surely ‘a’ is a “full word”?? Many letters’ names, or parts thereof, as sung, sound like “full” words. And we crossword puzzle solvers certainly know that letters’ names frequently appear here as crossworthy words.

Then, there is the issue of whether you sing the word “AND” before any other non-letter words.

So, the accurate clue would have been “First word that is not also the name of a letter, or part of the name of a letter, sung in the version of “The Alphabet Song” most widely familiar in the opinion of the constructor and editors.” Much better!

@Steve L This is cool! Never looked at these before. Wonder how much the stats change by this time tomorrow. Are people solving Saturday puzzles at midnight-ish on Friday a representative sample?
@Larg The times on xwstats are not representative at all. It's people who bother to link their accounts and upload stats, which isn't going to be the average solver by some margin.

@Larg

No data is ever perfect; a quarterback can lead the league in completions without ever throwing a pass of more than seven yards. As long as you understand the utility of the stat, as well as its limitations, you can derive some meaning from it.

If you are an occasional golfer, and you are at a hole that is designated "par 3," does that mean you are expected to shoot par most of the time? These designations are set with expert players in mind, and yet they still can give a duffer an accurate representation of the relative difficulty of the hole. You know it's easier than a par 5, even if you're likely to need 6 or 7 strokes instead of the designated 3.

Similarly, the xwstats.com data informs you, fairly accurately, I feel, about the relative difficulty of the puzzle. The stated "median solve time" is like the par designation. It only represents those who have linked their stats. You shouldn't think of it as where you should be, or be upset it you're not at that level.

I'd also like to point out that the cohort who links their stats may not necessarily be the most elite solvers. Rather, I think they are very committed solvers, more likely elite than not, but who also are computer-savvy, comfortable with linking sites, and willing to do so. I know many smart people who get flustered doing complicated things on the computer, and I'm not sure there's any correlation between willingness to link and puzzle-solving expertise.

Plus, there's no better indicator out there.
